verses.text: Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle (sent one) of Jesus Christ. I am sent according to the faith of God's elect (chosen people). I am sent for the acknowledging (knowing) of the truth which is after godliness.
This is in hope of eternal life. God, who cannot lie, promised it before the world began.
But in due times (at the right time) God has manifested (shown) His word through preaching. That preaching is committed (trusted) to me. It is according to the commandment of God our Saviour.
To Titus, my own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.
For this cause I left you in Crete. You should set in order the things that are wanting (lacking). You should ordain (appoint) elders in every city, as I had appointed you.
Ordain (appoint) one who is blameless, the husband of one wife. His children must be faithful, not accused of riot (wild living) or unruly (out of line).

For a bishop (church leader) must be blameless, as the steward (manager) of God. The bishop must not be selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine. The bishop must be no striker (violent), not given to filthy lucre (dishonest money).
But the bishop must be a lover of hospitality (welcoming strangers), a lover of good men. The bishop must be sober (clear-minded), just (fair), holy, temperate (self-controlled).

The bishop must hold fast the faithful word as he has been taught. Then he may be able by sound (healthy) doctrine (teaching) to exhort (encourage). The bishop may convince the gainsayers (those who argue against it).
For there are many unruly (out of line) and vain talkers (empty talkers) and deceivers. This is specially those of the circumcision (the circumcised Jews).
Their mouths must be stopped. They subvert (overturn) whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's (dishonest money's) sake.
One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said: The Cretians are always liars, evil beasts, slow bellies (lazy gluttons).
This witness is true. So rebuke (scold) them sharply, that they may be sound (healthy) in the faith.
They should not give heed (attention) to Jewish fables (made-up stories). They should not heed commandments of men, that turn from the truth.
To the pure all things are pure. But to those who are defiled (made unclean) and unbelieving nothing is pure. Even their mind and conscience is defiled (made unclean).
They profess (claim) that they know God. But in works they deny Him. They are abominable (hateful), and disobedient, and to every good work reprobate (worthless, rejected).

verses.text: But you speak the things which become (are right for) sound (healthy) doctrine (teaching).
The aged men should be sober (clear-minded), grave (serious), temperate (self-controlled). They should be sound (healthy) in faith, in charity (love), in patience.
The aged women likewise should be in behaviour as becomes (is right for) holiness. They should not be false accusers, not given to much wine. They should be teachers of good things.
Then they may teach the young women to be sober (clear-minded). They teach them to love their husbands, to love their children,
To be discreet (wise), chaste (pure), keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands. Then the word of God will not be blasphemed (spoken against).
Young men likewise exhort (encourage) to be sober minded (clear-minded).
In all things show yourself a pattern of good works. In doctrine (teaching) show uncorruptness (purity), gravity (seriousness), sincerity (with an honest heart).
Show sound (healthy) speech, that cannot be condemned (judged guilty). Then those of the contrary part (other side) may be ashamed. They will have no evil thing to say of you.
Exhort (encourage) servants to be obedient to their own masters. They should please them well in all things, not answering again (talking back).
They should not purloin (steal small things). But they should show all good fidelity (faithfulness). Then they may adorn (make beautiful) the doctrine (teaching) of God our Saviour in all things.
For the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all people.
It teaches us to deny ungodliness and worldly lusts (wrong desires). We should live soberly (with a clear mind), righteously (rightly), and godly, in this present world.
We look for that blessed hope. We look for the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ.
Christ gave Himself for us, that He might redeem (buy back and set free) us from all iniquity (sin). He would purify to Himself a peculiar (special, His own) people, zealous (eager) of good works.
Speak these things, and exhort (encourage), and rebuke (scold) with all authority. Let no one despise (look down on) you.

verses.text: Put them in mind to be subject to principalities (rulers) and powers. Remind them to obey magistrates (officials), to be ready to every good work,
To speak evil of no one, to be no brawlers (fighters), but gentle. Remind them to show all meekness (gentleness) to all people.

For we ourselves also were sometimes (once) foolish, disobedient, deceived (fooled). We served divers (many kinds of) lusts (wrong desires) and pleasures. We lived in malice (hate) and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
But then the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward people appeared.

God saved us, not by works of righteousness (being right with God) which we have done. God saved us according to His mercy. He saved us by the washing of regeneration (new birth), and renewing (making new) of the Holy Spirit.
God shed the Holy Spirit on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour.
We are justified (made right with God) by His grace. So we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

This is a faithful saying. I will that you affirm (strongly say) these things constantly. Then those who have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable (helpful) to people.
But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies (family lists), and contentions (fighting), and strivings about the law. For they are unprofitable (useless) and vain (empty).
After the first and second admonition (warning), reject a man who is an heretick (one who causes splits).
Know that such a one is subverted (turned aside), and sins. Such a one is condemned (judged guilty) of himself.
When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, be diligent (hurry) to come to me to Nicopolis. For I have determined to winter there.
Bring Zenas the lawyer (expert in God's law) and Apollos on their journey diligently (carefully). Make sure that nothing is wanting (lacking) to them.
And let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses. Then they will not be unfruitful.
All who are with me salute (greet) you. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
